sourceRefs.locator: Chapter 24, Armenian-era year 513, especially printed pp. 163–165 (Armenian pp. 134–136): two places of refuge, provisions, burial and usury. Chapter 25, pp. 167–171 (Armenian pp. 137–140): the names used for the two rulers, the captive’s release and his blinding.

§1.d, geographical coordinates of the property (40°30′ N, 43°34′ E), and §3, Justification for Inscription, account of the Bagratid capital, Byzantine takeover in 1045, capture by Alp Arslan in 1064 and subsequent Shaddadid rule.
Author manuscript, discussion of the five city accounts including Ani, pp. 16–20, with particular attention to debt, interest, scriptural models and the differing urban societies depicted.
